title: [C14T4] - Grange Park
prompt: The plans below show a public park when it first opened in 1920 and the same park today. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The two maps illustrate the changes that occurred in Grange Park between 1920 and the present day.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, Grange Park has undergone major transformations during this period, with numerous facilities being added, removed, or relocated. The most significant changes include the introduction of modern recreational facilities and the removal of several original features such as the fountain and glasshouse.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at the central and western areas of the park, the fountain that was positioned in the center in 1920 has been completely removed and replaced by a significantly enlarged rose garden surrounded by seats. The stage for musicians on the left side has been converted into a much larger amphitheatre for concerts, maintaining its entertainment function but with increased capacity. Meanwhile, the rose garden in the bottom-left corner has been eliminated to accommodate this expansion.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: On the eastern side, several notable changes have occurred. The rose garden and pond for water plants in the top-right area have been removed to make way for a café and children's play area, reflecting modern recreational needs. In the bottom-right corner, the glasshouse has been demolished and replaced by a water feature. Additionally, the seating area that once ran along the eastern edge has been converted into an underground car park entrance, with access from Eldon Street, addressing contemporary transportation requirements.
